subject.title: feat(codex): config to disable or scope the native hook relay (#91009)

question: Should the bundled Codex plugin permit `nativeHookRelay.enabled: false` and arbitrary event scopes when those choices can remove native hook processing that may carry approval or policy enforcement?
rationale: This is a product and security-boundary decision about the permanent operator contract, not a mechanical defect that contributor automation can safely choose.

options.title: Define a constrained supported policy
options.body: Specify which events remain mandatory, whether full disablement is allowed, and merge one narrow configuration implementation with live proof.

options.title: Allow full operator override
options.body: Document that disabling the relay intentionally removes native hook protections and accept the operational and security trade-off.

options.title: Keep relay policy internal
options.body: Reject new user configuration and continue addressing fan-out through the default relay implementation instead.

recommendation.title: Define a constrained supported policy
recommendation.body: Specify which events remain mandatory, whether full disablement is allowed, and merge one narrow configuration implementation with live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the only evidence-backed adjacent contributor identified in the supplied relay implementation history; an actual Codex-area owner should confirm the final contract.
